newsitem.title: USA: Cosbys to tabloids - drop rewards in son's slaying.
newsitem.headline: Cosbys to tabloids - drop rewards in son's slaying.

text.p: Entertainer Bill Cosby and his wife Camille, accusing tabloids of printing lies and being cruel, appealed to them on Tuesday to withdraw huge reward offers in the hunt for the murderer of the Cosbys' son, Ennis.
"I insist that all tabloid publications withdraw their rewards regarding our son's murder," said a statement by Camille Cosby released through the couple's spokesman David Brokaw.
"My husband and I do not want their money to be associated with our son," she said of offers of $100,000 by the National Enquirer and $200,000 by the Globe.

"These publications have lied about me and my family and they have enriched their coffers at our expense," Mrs. Cosby said. "Their treatment of our story is abusive, cruel, inhumane and overtly sexist."
There was no immediate response from the tabloids.

In fact, after Ennis Cosby's shooting in the early hours of Jan. 16 as he changed a tire by the side of a Los Angeles freeway, Bill Cosby had challenged the supermarket tabloids to put up money as a reward rather than pay for stories about the family and their murdered son.
In a related development on Tuesday, the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors voted to rescind the $12,500 reward it had offered to help catch 27-year-old Ennis Cosby's killer.

Supervisor Yvonne Brathwaite Burke, who jointly submitted the proposal to the Board last week, said it was in response to the Cosby family's request that taxpayer money not be used to post a reward in the case.
Last week the Cosbys asked the state of California and Los Angeles officials to rescind rewards totalling $87,500.
Camille Cosby ended her statement on Tuesday saying, "my energy remains focused on solving our son's murder and healing this horrific tragedy."
Los Angeles police have reported no breakthroughs in the case.
